notes.summary: Draft reconstruction of intrinsic roots and the signed genuine energy formula E_eta=(n+1)S_chi(eta)/n for all primary FS presentations and all Reeb fields, with effective grading, radial calibration, finite-map degree and signed residue errors. This does not prove uniform differentiation.
notes.detailedSummary: The argument independently reconstructs the supplied root and norm constructions rather than trusting the embedded round55 notes. The rational energy bridge uses normal full section rings, actual line-bundle frames, CLD fiber currents with one-unit Gauss mass, the degree-d Veronese cover, and BHJ model/DH energy compatibility. A homogeneous rank-d free Rees submodule and a common homogeneous denominator yield filtered injections and O(m^n) signed cutoff errors. Rational index clearing is valuation dilation/base change, not multiplication of a potential. Real weights and irrational Reeb fields pass through signed-mean and genuine local-uniform CLD energy continuity. These are unverified draft mathematical claims; the whole original target is not claimed.
notes.text:
Work on a normal good integral affine cone R of dimension n>=1 over any algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field. Sources are the ten exact public caches in the input, especially Wu2406.13684v1 (A), BJ1801.08229v4 (C), CLD1204.6277v2 (G), BHJ1504.06568v3 (H), and BE1805.01016v3 (J). No embedded generated note is a premise.

Let d_theta(alpha)=<theta,alpha>, choose fixed homogeneous algebra generators h_i with weights beta_i, and set K={v=q(v):min_i v(h_i)=0}. This is a compact closed subset of the coordinate unit polydisc. The actual torified action is (v+t eta)(sum f_alpha)=min_alpha(v(f_alpha)+t d_eta(alpha)). The reference rho_theta=max_i[-v(h_i)/d_theta(beta_i)] has section s_theta(v)=v+rho_theta(v)theta in K. Every theta-equivariant potential obeys u(v)=u(s_theta(v))+rho_theta(v). A primary FS list has some member of value zero at every point of K: otherwise expressing a zero-valued h_i^r in that primary ideal would give positive value. Thus all zero-weight primary references agree.

Every supported weight is a nonnegative integer combination of beta_i. Consequently c=min_i d_eta(beta_i)/d_xi(beta_i) and C=max_i of those ratios control all weights. Actual FS inequalities pass through uniform and decreasing completions to u(v)-Ct<=u(v+t eta)<=u(v)-ct for t>=0, and the reverse inequalities hold too. At finite points the orbit has a unique zero; at a minus-infinite point the whole orbit is minus infinity. Its zero parameter defines R_xi,eta u. For a primary presentation it is exactly max_j[(lambda_j-v(f_j))/d_eta(alpha_j)], so it is presentation independent. Uniform errors move roots by at most their error divided by c. At a finite limiting root, bracket it by two orbit points; at a minus-infinite limit use v-M eta for arbitrary M. These arguments give actual H/CPSH/PSH membership and preservation of defining decreasing nets. Equal zero sets give inverse and cocycle. Sup_K u=u(v_triv) is finite; normalized roots remain normalized. The raw map does not descend modulo constants: for k[x,y], xi=(1,1), eta=(1,2), R(rho_xi+2)-rho_eta takes values 2 and 1 at v_triv and (3,0). No quasi-monomial or strong-topology assertion follows from the full-pointwise continuity proof.

For algebra generators g_i with signed real assigned lambda_i, define F^a R_alpha as the span of monomials of weight alpha with assigned weight >=a, and chi(f) as its greatest index. There are finitely many monomials per weight space. This is a quotient filtration retaining relations, multiplicative and linearly bounded: chi(f)/d_theta(f) lies between the smallest and largest generator weight/degree ratios. Replacing lambda_i by chi(g_i) leaves the filtration unchanged: larger assigned weights give one inclusion, and multiplicativity gives the reverse. Its exact potential is sup_f(chi(f)-v(f))/d_theta(f)=max_i(lambda_i-v(g_i))/d_theta(g_i). For the upper bound use an expression attaining chi(f), the valuation inequality, and the weighted-average formula for each monomial; for the lower use each g_i. Infinite evaluations cause no exception. Append sufficiently negative algebra generators to any primary list: a primary member of value zero gives a uniform lower potential bound on a compact Reeb slice, and the appended terms can be placed below it. This changes no potential anywhere.

For rational eta=s eta_e use the effective integer grading of gcd one. Choose a sufficiently divisible degree d so R^(d) and the rational-index-cleared Rees Veronese are generated in new degree one. Generation can be proved by extracting generator powers of a common degree d0, bounding residual monomial degree, and choosing d divisible by d0 larger than that residual bound. A=R^(d)=R^(mu_d) is normal. Its inclusion in R is finite, and the faithful mu_d character decomposition gives degree d on fraction fields, with all d residues present. V=Proj R is normal. Actual degree-one localizations are A[a^-1]=A[a^-1]_0[a,a^-1], identifying the punctured standard cone with L_d^-1 minus zero. For n>=2, the height-one intersection characterization of a normal domain gives Hartogs across the vertex and A_l=H^0(V,l L_d). In dimension one the effective normal good ring is k[z] and V is a point.

Restriction of the norm to A has the same potential after scaling: the full supremum gives the upper inequality; powers of each primary generator lying in A give the lower. If p:Spec R->Spec A, then p*Phi=sd u_eta and p*rho_d=sd rho_eta, including positive parts. In a genuine L_d frame write Phi=log|t|+h, rho=log|t|+h0, where t has fiber degree one. If e_j=a_ij e_i, then t_j=a_ij t_i and h0,j=h0,i-log|a_ij|; the Gauss point below is frame independent. Tensor the projective FS bundles by their actual section exponents for CLD's integer-paralinear hypothesis; real constants are permitted by G12.5.2.

G18.6.1 on the flat torsor, with separated, equidimensional, boundaryless analytifications, says the horizontal top current equals sum_v a_v delta_(Y_v), where sum a_v delta_v is the actual projective mixed curvature measure. On its H(v)-fiber G18.6.2 gives ddc max(log|t|+h0(v),0) one unit Dirac mass at radius exp(-h0(v)). Smooth convex approximation and G8.7.2 therefore give the full measure identity against every local smooth test q: integral q T ddc rho^+=sum_v a_v q(i(v)). Partition of unity and G6.2.6 give all continuous local tests. The theorem includes singular bases; smoothness is not inferred. Uniform FS limits use the same weighted continuity. The total mass is (L_d^(n-1)), and each energy term is the projective one.

G13.3.7 gives calibrated degree d for the finite cover because the target is reduced. G16.1.5 therefore gives one factor d after n curvature/radial factors 1/(sd). The raw mass is V_eta=s^(-n)d^(1-n)(L_d^(n-1)), transverse class omega_eta=L_d/(sd), and normalized energy is E_Ld/(sd). Homogeneous values in R are uniquely recovered from their dth powers in A; finite-map surjectivity then gives the unique torified lift and the homeomorphism of compact carriers. Projective and cone probability measures agree under it. A section of mL cannot replace a degree-one frame without its radial 1/m.

For integral indices the finitely generated Rees filtration of the full section ring gives an ample test configuration by H2.15. The section maximum is the norm's exact FS metric. Graph normalization preserves that metric, and H3.14 preserves DH because V is reduced. H5.9 identifies the degree-wise spectral limit with DH, and linear boundedness permits signed first moments. H3.12(iii), H7.2--7.4 and H6.7 identify that mean with genuine normalized projective energy: model measure coefficients are b_E times mixed intersections divided by (L_d^(n-1)), while vertical coefficient r_E evaluates to r_E/b_E. There is no second volume division. J8.18/G18.4.7 give actual CLD/model compatibility. For rational indices b chi, the metric is b phi(v/b), not b phi(v); C7.2/7.7 and H6.3/6.13 give energy scaling by b under this base-change/valuation-dilation action. Dividing both mean and energy by b legitimately returns the rational filtration. Line-bundle tensoring is a separate operation.

The full-ring spectral step uses Gamma finite over B=Gamma^(d), of fraction rank d. Choose homogeneous e_j in each residue giving a free submodule F=sum B e_j, and clear the homogeneous fractions of a finite module generating set to obtain one homogeneous nonzero c with c Gamma subset F. Specializing at t=1 yields filtered injections F<=m -> R<=m and c R<=m -> F<=m+a with fixed degree/index shifts. A filtered injection increasing indices by b has descending weights w_i>=u_i+b; unmatched dimensions contribute at most their count times the linear O(m) weight bound. The injections bound dimension errors by O(m^(n-1)), hence total signed weight errors by O(m^n). Thus W_R(m)=d W_A(m/d)+O(m^n), with all residues accounted for; in dimension one the error is O(m), still negligible against mN(m). Degree-wise means e sum to the cumulative mean n e/(n+1), by Hilbert asymptotics and bounding the tail error by epsilon times l h^0(lL_d). Combining these facts with the genuine calibration proves E_eta=(n+1)S_chi(eta)/n at rational data.

For real weights, two filtration inclusions bound every spectral jump error by epsilon times its degree. The exact own-degree shift identity is W_shift=W+A D, where D=mN(m)-integral_0^m N(t)dt and D/(mN)->n/(n+1). For nonpositive lists, cutoff inclusions give W_xi(m/c)<=W_eta(m)<=W_xi(m/C). Rational approximation squeezes existence at irrational fields and yields exp(±(2n+1)delta) comparison of negative means, with delta=max_i |log degree-ratio|. Rational volume asymptotics and the same inclusions prove continuous positive volume at irrational fields. For arbitrary lists normalize by subtracting a(theta)d_theta, a(theta)=max lambda_i/d_theta(g_i); use the nonpositive comparison and perturbation bounds, then add back only the own-degree shift a(theta)n/(n+1). Finally G8.7.2 with moving radial currents and moving continuous energy weights proves genuine bounded/local-uniform mixed-MA and energy convergence on K. This passes the identity to all real weights and irrational fields and makes the mean presentation independent.

This is a mathematical draft argument, not a consequence of execution checks. Full details are in P13.1-argument.md Sections2--8 and standalone P13.1-paper.tex. Artifacts are in the current workspace. Rerun source auditing with python audit_sources.py; no previous campaign files are needed.

notes.summary: Using n1, normalized actual energies satisfy exp(±(2n+1)delta) comparison and roots preserve actual E1 through raw decreasing nets. A canonical outer energy agrees with existing energy, and its bounded-obstacle Reeb continuity has an explicit modulus. Differentiation remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: The signed representation turns finite cutoff inequalities into actual energy estimates uniform in potentials and presentations. Normalizing defining approximants does not preserve monotonicity, so the proof retains raw decreasing root images and bounds their energy differences from normalized images. The continuous-obstacle supremum F and usc outer extension F-downarrow are constructed from existing genuine energy, agree with it on CPSH and PSH respectively, and satisfy exact translation/Lipschitz bounds. Bounded-competitor truncation proves Reeb continuity. Rational residual torification proves equality of the torified and unrestricted projective energy suprema, but not their equality to volume.
notes.text:
Use the intrinsic roots, genuine energy identity, signed cutoff comparison, and bounded CLD continuity reconstructed in n1. Write delta=max_i|log(d_eta(beta_i)/d_xi(beta_i))|, k=2n+1, and normalize u by u(v_triv)=0. Then

exp(-k delta)(-E_xi(u)) <= -E_eta(R_xi,eta u) <= exp(k delta)(-E_xi(u)).

First prove this on primary FS by nonpositive weights and n1's E=(n+1)S/n, then on CPSH by uniform FS approximation and root Lipschitzness. Delta<=L_Q||eta-xi|| on a compact Reeb slice Q, where L_Q=max_i ||beta_i||_dual/min_(theta in Q)d_theta(beta_i); convex-hull segments retain these degree lower bounds. No constant depends on a presentation, potential, Veronese or rational denominator.

For actual PSH, same-Reeb decreasing energy continuity follows directly from its defining infimum over dominating CPSH: given w>=u and a defining u_i decreasing to u, the open sets {u_i<w+epsilon} cover compact K, so directedness gives u_i<=w+epsilon eventually. Monotonicity and translation, then infimum over w and epsilon->0, give E(u_i)->E(u), including minus infinity. If u is normalized E1, let a_i=u_i(v_triv) decrease to zero and v_i=u_i-a_i. The v_i need not decrease. Their energies tend to E(u), and the normalized comparison applies to each. The slope estimate bounds ||R u_i-R v_i||_K by |a_i|/c, which also bounds the same-field energy difference. The RAW roots R u_i decrease to R u and have energies bounded below. Decreasing energy continuity proves R u in E1 and the stated estimate. The inverse root proves onto on normalized constant quotients. No strong-topology theorem or moving-field unbounded mixed-measure tail theorem is claimed.

For continuous g on K define F_eta(g)=sup{E_eta(w):w in CPSH(eta), w|K<=g}. The reference plus min g is feasible and all competitors are below the reference plus max g. Therefore min g<=F(g)<=max g. Monotonicity, exact translation F(g+a)=F(g)+a and |F(g)-F(g')|<=||g-g'|| follow. If g is an actual CPSH restriction u, the competitor u and energy monotonicity give F(g)=E(u).

For ||g||<=M, replace each competitor by max(w,rho_eta-M), which preserves CPSH and feasibility and increases energy. Thus bounded competitors -M<=w|K<=M suffice. With a=w(v_triv), Nw=w-a, one has |a|<=M and -2M<=Nw<=0. The raw constant-shift root bound is ||R(w)-R(Nw)-a||<=M(exp(delta)-1). Combining it with the normalized energy estimate gives an energy transfer error <=2M(exp(k delta)-1)+M(exp(delta)-1). Also ||Rw-w||<=M(exp(delta)-1). Subtract that last amount to regain feasibility, take suprema, and reverse the fields. The resulting actual modulus is

|F_eta(g)-F_xi(g)| <= 2M[exp(k delta)-1+exp(delta)-1].

It is locally uniform over bounded obstacles. An unbounded pointwise root comparison alone would not control this supremum.

On a rational quotient, the naturally linearized L_d has eigen-section charts. Componentwise minima define a continuous residual-torus torification q_V, compatible on overlaps. Its invariant canonical reference is unchanged. The Gauss section and unique torified finite lift identify K with its image. Splitting every section of a projective FS metric psi into residual weight components with its original coefficient gives an actual globally generating FS list for psi composed with q_V. Ultrametricity gives psi composed with q_V >= psi; uniform FS approximation gives the CPSH version. If g=g composed with q_V and psi<=g, the torified psi remains feasible. Monotonicity therefore proves equality of torified and unrestricted PROJECTIVE ENERGY suprema. No volume identity follows merely from obstacle invariance.

For upper-semicontinuous bounded-above h, put F_down(h)=inf{F(g):g continuous, g>=h}. This has exact translation, monotonicity and agrees with F on continuous obstacles. For defining u_i decreasing to actual PSH u, F_down(u)<=E(u_i). Conversely any continuous g>=u eventually bounds u_i up to epsilon by the compact open-cover argument, so E(u)<=F(g)+epsilon. Thus F_down(u)=E(u), including energy minus infinity. The identical argument for an arbitrary decreasing usc net proves continuity of F_down along such nets. In particular

F_down(u+t f)=lim_i F(u_i+t f), and |F_down(u+t f)-E(u)|<=|t| ||f||

for u in E1 and any continuous f. This is independent of the defining net. It constructs a genuine canonical energy extension without asserting an unproved E(P(u+t f)) equality. Agreement and translation bounds do not establish its derivative. The remaining differentiation gate is in n3.

Detailed arguments are in P13.1-argument.md Sections9 and12. The results are unverified mathematical drafts and do not close unchanged P13.1.

notes.summary: Derived the two-sided relative-volume remainder 2pA(1+A tau)^(p-1)||f|| t^2, with p=n-1, and a common dense carrier direction class. The indispensable obstacle-energy/volume reverse inequality on singular quotients remains unreconstructed, so this is not a cone energy derivative.
notes.detailedSummary: BGM Lemma3.2 has no envelope antecedent and works on geometrically reduced projective schemes over arbitrary complete NA fields. Its full reduction and restriction/RR proof are audited with actual raw factors. A single rational-FS lattice of directions on K is dense and has uniform positive domination in A omega_eta on compact Reeb slices. Nevertheless BE9.15 only supplies continuous-psh equality; its FS supnorm isometry does not supply leading signed-mean convergence of the generated higher-degree norms. BJ8.7 explicitly uses an additional asymptotic FS theorem absent from the ten bodies; the available supporting BJ1805.11160 theorem has standing smoothness and invokes an external lattice saturation result. Hence only relative-volume differentiation, not F_down cone differentiation, is established.
notes.text:
Use n1's calibrated rational quotient omega_eta=L_d/(sd), its genuine probability MA, and n2's actual energy supremum/outer extension.

Fix rational xi0 and let D be the rational linear span of differences of rational-weight primary FS functions at xi0 restricted to K. Allow arbitrary positive rational equivariant slope in intermediate expressions. Products after clearing exponents represent positive sums; maxima concatenate primary lists, and reference padding matches slopes. Every element can be written A0(phi-psi) for a positive rational A0 and two actual rational FS functions at xi0. The identity max(a-b,c-d)=max(a+d,c+b)-(b+d), permitting the common slope to increase and then rescaling, proves lattice closure; negation gives minima. Rational constants are reference translates. Distinct torified points differ on a homogeneous g; primary padding gives max((lambda-v(g))/d_xi0(g),-M) on K, which separates them for suitable rational lambda,M, including infinite valuations. The uniform closure is a real vector lattice separating points and containing constants, hence all C(K) by lattice Stone-Weierstrass. A single fixed-slope difference set is not assumed dense.

For f=A0(phi-psi), eta in compact Q, extend by f_eta(v)=f(v+rho_eta(v)eta). For a branch f_j,lambda_j of phi put r_j(eta)=A0 d_eta(f_j)/d_xi0(f_j), and choose one rational A exceeding all r_j for both lists and Q. Then

a_eta=max_j[A0(lambda_j-v(f_j))/d_xi0(f_j)+(A-r_j(eta))rho_eta],

with the analogous b_eta, has a_eta-b_eta=f_eta and equivariant slope A. For rational eta expand rho_eta over h_l. Each branch is a positive rational logarithmic sum c_j(lambda_j-v(f_j))-c_l v(h_l) with total eta degree A. Clearing logarithmic coefficients by m gives a monomial f_j^(mc_j)h_l^(mc_l) of eta/A degree m, and the assigned coefficient mc_j lambda_j. The list is primary because away from the vertex some primary f_j and some h_l are nonzero. Thus a_eta,b_eta are actual FS(eta/A). At irrational eta, rational approximants followed by roots back to the fixed eta/A change their uniformly bounded restrictions on K by o(1); the limit is actual CPSH(eta/A). Their difference on K is the single fixed f for every field. On the rational quotient the positivity class is A omega_eta and ||f|| is unchanged.

BGM2004.03847v1 (I), LF647--724, proves Lemma3.2 for geometrically reduced projective X, ample L, continuous psh phi on L, and continuous psh psi1,psi2 on an auxiliary ample M. With p=dim X, f=psi1-psi2, C=(L+M)^p-L^p,

C inf f <= integral f(ddc phi+ddc psi1)^p-vol(L,phi+f,phi) <= C sup f.

There is no envelope-continuity hypothesis. The full proof passes to an algebraically closed nontrivially valued extension, uses uniform nef-model approximation and a higher reduced-special-fiber model, perturbs toward ample models, and clears tensor powers. BE1805.01016v3 (J) Theorem6.6/Proposition9.12 and MA compatibility retain volumes and curvature under extension. Relatively regular sections exist by actual J PropositionA.15: flat projective finitely presented morphism and relative ampleness; prime avoidance on associated fiber points is its proof. Such sections restrict regularly to an effective vertical divisor by I1.2. Normalize inf f=0, making the vertical divisor E effective on the reduced special fiber by I1.3. Restriction exact sequences bound determinant volume by sum_(j=1)^m h^0(E,(mL+jE)|E) <= m h^0(E,m(L+M1)|E). I2.4 gives h^0(E,mN|E)=m^p/p! integral phi_E(ddc phi_N)^p+O(m^(p-1)), by Serre vanishing, the degree-p determinant difference, and Deligne/curvature compatibility. Dividing by m^(p+1)/p! gives the left estimate. Normalize sup f=0, use effective D=-E and sequences for mL-jD to obtain the right estimate. A constant shift moves the difference by aC, restoring the two-sided claim.

On the rational quotient apply this to epsilon psi1,epsilon psi2 with M=epsilon A omega, first for rational epsilon by tensor clearing and then by uniform metric continuity. Divide RAW volume by V=omega^p. The expanded positive measure V^(-1)(ddc phi+epsilon ddc psi1)^p is the original probability plus positive terms of total mass (1+epsilon A)^p-1. Bound both the source-estimate error and the added integral by epsilon times this mass times ||f||. For either sign of t, interchanging psi1 and psi2 for t<0, this yields

|vol(omega,phi+t f,phi)/V - t integral f MA_omega(phi)| <= 2|t|[(1+A|t|)^p-1]||f||
<= 2pA(1+A tau)^(p-1)||f|| t^2, for |t|<=tau and p>=1.

For p=0 the normal quotient is a point and the remainder is zero. The bound is potential independent and all Reeb dependence is absorbed into the one common A; no rational denominator appears. This is an actual RELATIVE-VOLUME bound.

The exact gap is the reverse inequality in

sup_(psi continuous psh, psi<=g) E_L(psi) = vol(L,g,h0)/(L^p)

for an arbitrary continuous obstacle on every normal possibly singular quotient. The <= direction follows from J Theorem9.15 and volume monotonicity. J Theorem9.15 identifies volume with energy only for TWO CONTINUOUS PSH metrics; Corollary9.16 separately assumes envelopes. J7.26/7.27 provide dominated supnorm FS approximants and degree-m supnorm isometry, but not leading determinant-mean convergence for the quotient norms they generate in all multiples of m. BJ1801.08229v4 (C), LF4888--4900, explicitly supplies the latter step through [Reb21, Theorem5.1.1], which is outside the ten permitted bodies. The supporting BJ1805.11160v1 (F) Theorem4.13 is under standing smooth-projective scope; its Lemma4.15 proof invokes an external lattice saturation lemma. No valid independent extension of that approximation proof to the present singular quotients is supplied here. The finite Rees-module argument of n1 compares Veroneses of ONE finite-type norm, and cannot replace approximation of an arbitrary obstacle graded norm by growing finite-type norms.

BJ Theorem8.5/Corollary8.6 at LF4843--4862 really do differentiate E-downarrow on every projective E1 potential WITHOUT an envelope hypothesis. The additional equality with E(P(.)) retains that hypothesis. Thus a singular envelope theorem is not made an artificial prerequisite; the actual gap here is the obstacle-volume approximation above. Its absence in this reconstruction is not evidence the asserted equality is false.

If a bounded cone F estimate were proved, n2's Reeb continuity and n1's bounded actual MA convergence would pass it to irrational fields. Decreasing outer continuity and the existing genuine same-Reeb mixed-MA continuity would then pass it to E1. For continuous f approximated by f_m in D, translation/Lipschitzness and probability mass give exactly the derivative-remainder quotient bound 2||f-f_m||+C_(Q,f_m)|t|, with m chosen before t. This is a transfer implication here, NOT an established cone derivative; it would not give a quadratic estimate for every continuous direction or uniformity over its unit ball.

Detailed proof and source bodies are in P13.1-argument.md Sections10--14 and source-extracts/source-provenance.json. The source proof corrections include the missing J subtraction and n-1 sum index in Wu, the cumulative n/(n+1) factor, the extra volume division in BHJ Remark7.5, and BJ Cor8.6's extra t and incorrect upper-error sign. Uniform cone differentiation remains unresolved.

notes.text:
The mathematical claims and limits are n1--n3. The draft claims the genuine signed representation and normalized E1 comparison, a common dense direction class, canonical outer extension and bounded-obstacle Reeb continuity, and a both-sign uniform relative-volume bound. It does not prove the reverse continuous-obstacle energy/volume inequality on every singular rational quotient. Consequently it does not prove the required bounded cone differentiation estimate or its irrational/E1 extension. The unchanged original P13.1 is therefore NOT solved; candidate=false. P13.2 image and existence are untouched. No independent mathematical correctness or novelty verdict is asserted.
